# The ALGOL 60 harness

*Phase 4, wave 1, against `spec-1.0`. The per-system part of the harness for
ALGOL 60 (`systems/algol-60/README.md`), written to the common contract in
[`../README.md`](../README.md). Where the contract or the specification could
not be implemented as written for ALGOL 60, the reading taken is in
[`QUESTIONS.md`](QUESTIONS.md) (entries A1–A17).*

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `run` | the harness: `run CONFIGURATION PROBLEM INSTANCE MODE PROGRAM OUTDIR` |
| `check` | the syntax check, which executes nothing: `check CONFIGURATION PROGRAM` |
| `README.md` | this file: the program contract, per configuration, and how the harness works |
| [`S-mechanisms.md`](S-mechanisms.md) | the S mechanisms of each configuration (none) |
| [`QUESTIONS.md`](QUESTIONS.md) | what could not be implemented as written, and the reading taken |
| [`qualification/`](qualification) | the evidence that the harness does what this file says: `qualify.py`, its output, its made-up programs and stages file, and the records it wrote |

Both scripts are **Python 3.11, standard library only**, as the image
`cp-agent-systems:spec-1.0` provides it (`/usr/bin/python3`). They install
nothing. They run inside the image, from the repository root mounted at
`/work`:

    container run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --volume REPO:/work --workdir /work \
        cp-agent-systems:spec-1.0 harnesses/algol-60/run report P07 P07c behaviour PROGRAM OUTDIR

---

## 1. Configurations

| configuration | system run | modes | budget | stages received |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **report** | `/usr/local/bin/algol60` (`6e8740c`); storage mode `/usr/local/bin/algol60-measure` (`151cdff`) with `--measure` | behaviour, cost, storage | enforced, `--max-steps` | incremental or reposed, as the program declares (section 2.2) |
| **x1** | the same, with `--x1` | behaviour, cost, storage | enforced, `--max-steps` | as report |
| **x1sim** | `/usr/local/bin/x1sim` (`938fa03`), which compiles with `x1algc` and simulates | **behaviour only** | **not enforced** (`budget_enforced: false`): x1sim has no step count | incremental (one live process) or reposed |

The step unit is the interpreter's tick as `--max-steps` counts it
(`systems/algol-60/README.md`, Units). `run` refuses `cost` and `storage` for
x1sim (exit 2). The configuration never chooses incremental or reposed
posing from a result: the program declares it before it is run.

**Can a configuration continue after budget?** No, in report and x1: when
`--max-steps` fires the interpreter stops the program with an error and the
process ends, so there is no computation to pose stage k+1 into. Stage k+1
is reposed (`reason: "after-budget"`). x1sim has no budget.

---

## 2. The program contract

An author who cannot run the program before its results are taken writes it
to this section, and may use only `check` (section 6) before it is fixed.

### 2.1 File layout

- **One file**, the whole program: one ALGOL 60 program (a block or compound
  statement). Any extension; the harness copies it as `prog.a60` for x1sim.
- **Constants** (common contract, section 11.6): every constant of every stage
  is in **one input file**, beside the program, with the same name and the
  extension `.constants` (`P07c.alg` → `P07c.constants`). The verifier
  substitutes a hidden variant by passing another file in the environment
  variable `ALGOL60_CONSTANTS` (and its id in `ALGOL60_VARIANT`); the program
  is not touched. **Every line of the file is tagged with the stage that
  first uses it**: `k: v1 v2 …`, where k is a stage of the instance (1..K)
  and the values are integers in the problem's encoding
  (`systems/algol-60/README.md`, Values), separated by spaces, in a layout the
  program states in a comment. A stage may have several lines, or none;
  blank lines are ignored; any other line is refused (exit 2). The harness
  sends stage k's lines **only with the message that poses or replays stage
  k** (2.2): no stage's constants are on the program's input before that
  stage is posed (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Writing a program", rule 5, no
  anticipation). A constant a later stage uses again is kept by the program
  from the stage that first gave it. The program must stay correct for other
  constants: give lengths in the file, never in the program. A sub-problem with no constants has no file (`constants.how =
  "none"`). The program holds nothing else of the stages.
- **Representation**:
  - *report*: as `algol60` reads it: reserved words in lower case
    (`begin`, `if`), or quote-stropped, or underlined; strings `"..."` (with
    `\n`) or `` `...' ``. The procedures `ininteger`, `outinteger`,
    `outstring` are IFIP's, and are external mechanisms in report
    (systems file, Configurations).
  - *x1sim*: as the X1 compiler reads it: **underlined reserved words**
    (each letter followed by U+0332, `b̲e̲g̲i̲n̲`), strings only `` `...' ``,
    the operators as symbols (`¬ ∧ ∨ ⊃ ≡ ≠ ≤ ≥ × ÷`; underlined `not` or `and`
    are refused), and the X1 system's procedures `read`, `print`,
    `PRINTTEXT`, `NLCR`, `SPACE`, `TAB` (no `ininteger` or `outstring`).
    Characters in strings: letters, digits, space and `[ ] / = : , . ( ) + -`
    (the X1 code has no `#`, `@`, `<` inside text is risky). The X1 system
    breaks a line at 144 positions: print `NLCR` between answers so that
    no tag is split.
  - *x1*: `algol60 --x1` reads both forms and has both sets of procedures.
    A program in the x1sim form runs unchanged in x1 (the qualification does
    this); a program in the report form runs in x1 too.
- **Declarations, in comments** (comments are not tokens). An ALGOL 60
  comment ends at the first `;`, so none of these may contain `;`:

      comment HARNESS POSING incremental;          (or: reposed — exactly one, required)
      comment PROVENANCE author: ...;
      comment PROVENANCE precursor seen: yes|no;
      comment PROVENANCE idioms: <each idiom and its source>;
      comment CONSTANTS <the layout of the constants file>;

  `run` and `check` read the posing declaration from the program's bytes,
  and refuse a program without exactly one (exit 2).

### 2.2 How the program learns which stage to handle: its input

The harness writes everything on the program's **standard input**, as lines
of integers, read with the configuration's input procedure
(`ininteger(0, v)` in report and x1; `v := read` in x1 and x1sim):

1. **The instance line**, first: `n a m c1 … cm`
   - `n` the instance's size (`stages.json` parameter `n`), else 0;
   - `a` its answer cap where the instance gives one (P12: 20 for `all`,
     1 for `any-one`), else 0;
   - `m` the number of codes that follow, and `c1 … cm` the instance's
     `order` or `spawn_order`, each as its code (table below), else `m = 0`.
2. **Messages**, one per line, each **followed by the constants lines of
   the stage it poses or replays** (the lines of the file tagged `k:`, in
   file order, with the tag removed and the values verbatim; nothing if the
   stage has none). The program reads exactly that stage's constants after
   reading the message's words:

   | message | meaning |
   |---|---|
   | `1 k` | **pose stage k**: stage k's information arrives (in an incremental program, into the computation that holds stages 1..k−1; in a reposed run, the stage posed after the replay) |
   | `2 j` | **replay stage j** (reposed run only): carry out stage j again, as when it was posed, replacements and withdrawals included |
   | `3 j` then a line `v` | **replay commit stage j as the information x = v** (P11, reposed run): `v` is the commit stage's first answer, verbatim as it was printed (the text between `[answer]` and `[/answer]`), then stage j's constants lines. Print P11 answers so that they can be read back (as integers) |
   | `4 k c` | **spawn computation c of stage k** (P09a, P09b): start computation c and run it to its end; stage k's constants follow each spawn message |

   The program answers **every message with exactly one `[end]`** (2.3),
   printed when it has finished with that message, and then reads its next
   message. It never reads input beyond the message it is handling: in an
   incremental run the next message is written only after `[end]`, so a read
   beyond it waits forever (and the stage ends at the safety limit). After the
   last stage the harness closes the input; the program's next read then
   fails with the interpreter's "the input is exhausted" (x1sim: "No input"),
   which ends the process. That is expected, not an error of the stage.

   No message says how many stages follow (no anticipation).

**Incremental program** (`HARNESS POSING incremental`; the systems file's
"read each stage with ininteger or insymbol as it arrives, which counts as
the same computation"): a loop that reads a message, handles it, prints the
stage's answers and observe block, prints `[end]`, and reads the next. It
must also accept `2 j` and `3 j` (handled as `1 j`, and as x = v): the
harness reposes an incremental program after a budget, error or safety stop.
Stage 1 arrives as `1 1`.

**Reposed program** (`HARNESS POSING reposed`; "otherwise each stage is
posed by rerunning with stages 1 to k"): for stage k the harness starts the
program afresh and writes, at once, `2 1` … `2 k−1` (with `3 j` + `v` for a
commit stage) and then `1 k`. The program reads messages until it reads a
`1`, printing `[end]` after each replayed one, then computes stage k, prints
its answers and observe block and a final `[end]`, and may end.

Codes of `order`, `spawn_order` and computations (by first appearance in
`stages.json`; structure, not constants):

| instance or stage | what | codes |
|---|---|---|
| P02b | `order` | R1 = 1, R2 = 2, R3 = 3 |
| P07a | `order` | 1 = 1, 2 = 2, 3 = 3 |
| P09a, P09b | `spawn_order` | A = 1, B = 2 |
| P09a, P09b stage 1 | computation `c` of `4 1 c` | A = 1, B = 2 |
| P16a | `order` | ascending = 1, descending = 2, interleaved = 3 |
| P16b, P16c, P16d, P16d2 | `order` | ascending = 1 |
| P16b stage 1 | computations C1–C4 | **not spawned**: posed as `1 1` to `main` (`spawn_fallback`, QUESTIONS.md A3) |

So `P12c.n16.any` gives the line `16 1 0`, `P09a.BA` gives `0 0 2 2 1`
followed by `4 1 2` and later `4 1 1`, and `P16a.n100.descending` gives
`100 0 1 2`.

### 2.3 How the program reports: tags in its output

Answers reach the harness through the system's standard mechanism, the values
the program prints (systems file; `PROTOCOL.md`). The program prints them,
with `outstring`/`outinteger` (report) or `PRINTTEXT`/`print` (x1sim), between
these tags. The harness keeps the text between tags **verbatim** (the
padding of `outinteger` and of the X1 `print` included):

| tag | meaning |
|---|---|
| `[answer]TEXT[/answer]` | one answer to the query of the computation now running. In order; the first `cap` are collected (`stages.json` gives the cap of each query), any more stay in `stdout` and `print` |
| `[observe]TEXT[/observe]` | the state for `observe()` at the end of the stage (2.4). Print it once, after the answers |
| `[emit]TEXT[/emit]` | the effect stub `emit(TEXT)` (P11, 2.5) |
| `[end]` | the program has finished with the current message. Print a newline *before* it, nothing after it before the next read |

The text of a tag must not contain the tags themselves.

### 2.4 observe() and the execution state

ALGOL 60 has no unknowns, alternatives or suspension of its own, so
`observe()` reads what the program prints in its observe block, and the
execution state is read from it. Inside `[observe]…[/observe]`, any text
(the held relations, a residual, the program's named structures) is kept
verbatim in `observe.raw`; these tags are also read mechanically:

| inside observe | recorded as |
|---|---|
| `[bind NAME]VALUE[/bind]` | `observe.bindings[NAME] = VALUE` |
| `[alternatives NAME COUNT]` | `alternatives.by_type[NAME]`; `at_boundary` is their sum; a sum above 0 is the state **alternatives pending** |
| `[held-as all-live]` (`backtracking`, `mixed`) | `alternatives.held_as` (else `unknown` if alternatives are reported, `none` if not) |
| `[problem-alternatives NAME COUNT]` | `alternatives.problem_defined[NAME]` (METRICS.md: P05's values of x, P12's partial sequences, P15a's interleavings) |
| `[suspended NAME COUNT]` | `suspended.items[NAME]`; `at_boundary` their sum; a sum above 0 is the state **suspended** |
| `[operations NAME COUNT]` | `problem_operations[NAME]`: applications of each case of each relation (`conc/1`), counted by the program **since the computation started** |
| `[candidates COUNT]` | `candidates_examined` (P12) |

COUNT is an integer, printed with `outinteger` or `print` (a leading `+` and
spaces are accepted). A stage that ends with `[end]` (or with the program's
normal end) and reports neither alternatives nor suspended work is
**finished**. **budget**: the interpreter reported `stopped after N steps`.

log is `OUTDIR/<instance>.effects.jsonl` in behaviour mode, and
`OUTDIR/<instance>.effects-observation.jsonl` in cost and storage mode; it
is never reset. The interpreter holds its output until it next reads input
(or ends), so an emit is logged by the end of its stage at the latest.

At a commit stage the program selects one outcome and prints it as the
stage's answer. That answer, verbatim, is v: a later reposed run sends
`3 j` and then v on its own line, and the program takes it as x = v without
selecting again.

### 2.6 spawn (P09a, P09b)

ALGOL 60 has no separate computations. A spawned computation is a part of
the one program (a procedure, typically), started by the message `4 k c`.
It runs to its end, budget or error, and prints `[end]`; then the harness
spawns the next, in the instance's `spawn_order` (`side_by_side: false`).
They share the program's variables. Each has its own budget (report, x1). If
one ends the process (budget, error, timeout), the ones after it in the stage
are recorded as not started (QUESTIONS.md A3).

### 2.7 H tokens

These constructs are **H** (`METRICS.md`, class H, rule 13), every token of
each:

1. each statement that reads a harness word: the instance line
   (`ininteger(0, n)`, `n := read`, the loop that reads the codes), a message
   word (code, stage number, computation code), and the statement that reads
   the replayed value v (turning v into the information x = v is classed by
   METRICS.md, not H);
2. the message loop: its `for … while …` header (or label and `go to`), and
   the tests and connectives that select by the message code, by k (which
   stage's code to run) and by c (which computation): the dispatch, not the
   stage code it selects;
3. every output statement whose only effect is to print a tag or the text
   inside a tag (`[answer]`, `[observe]` and its inner tags, `[emit]`,
   `[end]`, and the `NLCR` that separate them), and procedures whose only
   effect is to print answers or state the program already holds (output
   adapters);
4. counters that only count (problem operations, candidates): their
   declarations and increments;
5. declarations of variables that hold only harness words (the message code,
   the stage number k, the computation code c, a loop variable of the message
   loop).

Not H: the variables holding instance parameters as the program uses them
(n, an order, the cap), reading the constants (that is the stage
information, P), holding information between stages, and any pending or
suspension structure (R or S by METRICS.md rule 19).

### 2.8 A complete minimal example

Made-up problem **X01** (not one of P01–P16): one unknown integer x; stage 1
gives x ≥ c1, stage 2 gives x ≤ c2, stage 3 gives x ≠ c3; the query is every
x. Program `qualification/programs/x01-incremental.alg`, configuration

# Independent classifier B notes: ALGOL 60, P07–P08, batch 1B

I classified the public evidence independently. I did not write these programs, read another classifier's work, run an ALGOL program, run the interpreter/compiler/simulator, or use the web. The scope is the 1B P07–P08 text manifest and the corresponding batch-log runs; the brief's isolated reference to batch 1A was not used to expand that scope.

## Token decisions

The JSON uses the first path of each of the 16 texts in "'`TEXTS-1B-P07-P08.tsv`. The other 14 program paths inherit their text'"'s classes. I checked the frozen token sequences of every alias against the first path. No class differs between x1 and x1sim: different execution environments do not change the role of these constructs. Token indices always come from the supplied TSVs; no program was re-tokenized. The generated line maps preserve those indices.

Rule 19 is the principal boundary. Known flags, held flags, retirement of relations, and changed-pass bookkeeping implement holding for these particular equations, so they are R. The arithmetic evaluator's assignments and fully known relation tests are P in every direction, including divisibility and zero-factor checks. The fact that an evaluator branch is not visited on these constants does not change its class. For example, "'`report/P07c.alg` tokens 46–51 test knownness (R), 53–62 test the arithmetic relation and record inconsistency (P), and 73–77 compute the missing place (P). Its procedure framing remains R, with nested constructs split by rule 10.

Explicit pass/order loop headers are C, as are the order dispatch in P07a and permission conditions containing definition flags in P08. Tests of which places are known remain R under rule 19. This distinguishes a holding representation from the explicit decision about when to revisit it. A possible ambiguity is whether rule 19 should absorb the entire problem-specific propagation loop into R. I applied the explicit scheduling definition of C to its header and loop framing, while retaining its problem-specific held-state operations as R. Conditions such as a failure guard beyond the relation'"'s case test are also C under rule 2.

P07g is a harder rule 19 boundary. Computing a missing *single* multiplication place from the others is P; solving the repeated-place constraint "'`x*x=c1` by a square-root/sign algorithm is a changed algorithm, R. Thus proposing `entier(sqrt(c1)+0.5)`, choosing its signs and retaining the candidate list are R. Testing a fully known candidate'"'s square against c1 is P. The sign algorithm is not a search mechanism general over relations. Its two roots exhaust this instance because "'`(x-3)(x+3)=0` over the integers. The use of sqrt and entier is recorded here as built-ins used in that reformulation; the explicit square check guards the candidate result on this input. These records do not establish arbitrary-precision numerical reliability of the root algorithm for unlimited constants.

The sequence constructors, decomposition, and equality operations are P by the systems file'"'s encoding convention and rule 15. The recursive forward conc/rev cases are P by rule 3; their operation counters are H. P08c adds a three-state success/failure/missing-case protocol: its status return declaration, status locals, status assignment targets, status propagation and missing-case decisions are R, separated from the original relation applications. Permission flags and their gates are C. This is a case-specific implementation, not a general dynamic-definition interpreter.

Output adapters are H under rule 13 even when they walk a sequence or inspect held flags to print an existing state. The derived "'`held` count only serves observe output and is H too. No such adapter derives a missing solution. Fixed message loops, stage dispatch headers, harness-word input, unused harness-word variables, and operation counters are H under harness section 2.7. Reading a stage'"'s constants and constructing its encoded value are P. Main block framing belongs to the harness driver. Commas and semicolons introducing the next construct follow rule 20; mixed declarations and mixed chained initialization targets are split by role rather than assigning every declared variable the same class.

## Outcomes and residual equivalence

P07a computes (5,4,3) in all six orders by deciding one relation at a time; the operation counts differ by order. P07d computes w=7 by checked integer division. P07e explicitly detects that 2 does not divide 15. P07g prints both 3 and -3, retaining them together as computed answer values. It holds no request-for-more-answers continuation, so it is finished, not alternatives pending.

P07b retains the exact conjunction, which is equivalent to x=7,y=3 but reducible. P07c retains the exact integer sum relation; its infinite set has a finite equivalent residual and is reduced by the specification's explicit example. P07f retains two contradictory sum equations; its denotation is correctly empty but the inconsistency is undetected. These are program-held flags and evaluators, not strings printed in place of state. The records' suspended classification is used even for these one-stage programs whose process then exits, consistently with the harness's stage-boundary observation contract.

P08a/b keep equality constraints rather than identifying element unknowns. At stages 4 and 5 the reversed sequence is already computed, but x=y, and later y=z, remain to be decided. They are therefore residual and reducible, not solved form. Stage 6 propagates 42 through all three element slots and reaches the explicit solution. P08c holds the application at stage 3: its enabled empty-input case does not cover (1,2), and the missing recursive case leaves it pending. Stage 4 yields (2,1). Neither a manual reapplication nor a manual intervention appears in any record.

**P08 under the closed reading is a deliberately explicit denotational decision.** I interpret the relation actually retained in the residual under each requested reading. With no rev cases, or only the empty-input case applied to (1,2), that residual denotes the empty set under the closed reading. I therefore class it complete / residual / inconsistency undetected, not an unsound explicit claim of a free b. This does **not** mean the program detected failure or adopted undefined-as-false: its printed state is pending, neither true nor false. The distinction between that operational state and the closed denotation is preserved in every entry's equivalence reasoning and observations. A competing interpretation would treat “awaiting its definition” as an assertion of future possibility rather than as a retained relation, yielding unsound under the closed reading. The problem does not explicitly settle this pending-residual case under the closed reading; I used the specification's general rule that equivalent empty residual conditions are complete even when their inconsistency is undetected, as in P07f.

Under the open reading, pending rev contributes no restriction on current values. A smaller *current-stage* representation can therefore omit that pending condition, giving a solved form with b free; at stage 3 it can also identify x with y. I mark those residuals reducible. Dropping the application would lose future work, which is a separate operational observation. This exposes another ambiguity: if “smaller equivalent” were required to preserve future resumption as well as current valid outcomes, a lone pending application could instead be called reduced. I applied the stated current-stage denotational equivalence criterion.

For residual sizes I count the primitive relation applications still undecided and unknown occurrences in those applications, alongside the cumulative input equations/applications. Definitions and already solved binding terms are recorded separately. Arithmetic compounds would be decomposed with fresh unknowns, although no surviving residual here has compound arithmetic. A named rev application counts once. "'`identical_to_posed` compares with cumulative posed information, not merely the most recent addition: P07b/c/f and P08c'"'s untouched application are true; P08a/b are false after a was bound and substituted into the application. The latter convention is another possible boundary if one instead compares only the unresolved portion of the input.

The algebraic and symbolic substitution checks in "'`check_result.py` accompany the by-hand universal reasoning in the JSON. They manipulate mathematical values/terms only, never evaluate the submitted programs, and do not use bounded enumeration as a proof about an unbounded domain.

## Definition arrival, expressibility and supporting mechanisms

All nine configuration/program P08 combinations await **permission**, not code. The source already contains rev/conc and the case bodies. The stages set `defined`, or `concdef`, `rev1def`, `rev2def`; P08c also receives the base-fact sequences as data at stage 3. Token ranges for the compiled bodies, gates and stage updates are given in `late_definition`. A changed Boolean is not a definition body arriving. P08b leaves the permission disabled and keeps its application distinguishable from failure.

I judge each staged subproblem expressible with reformulation in each configuration: the problem-specific R representation preserves the relation'"'s meaning, while the forward sequence cases themselves are transcriptions. This judgement concerns the staged mathematical relation, not the capability to deliver new procedure code, which these programs do not demonstrate. Hidden variants were inaccessible and were not checked; the numerical limitation of P07g above remains a limitation of the evidence. There is no evidence here of a separate variant program beyond the 30 paths in the text manifest and batch log.

There are **no S mechanisms and no S tokens** in any of the following programs, in each of report ("'`.alg`), x1 (`.a60`) and x1sim (`.a60`): P07a, P07b, P07c, P07d, P07e, P07f, P07g, P08a, P08b, P08c. Consequently `s_mechanisms` is empty. Phase 4 lists none supplied. The programs supply specific equation holders, element-equality holding, a pending-rev flag and (in P08c) case-availability status, all R rather than a reusable general relation store, unifier, loader, or scheduler. The broad example “wait-for-definition layer” in the S definition is potentially ambiguous here; I use rule 19'"'s more specific distinction by generality. I would classify a general reusable loader/dispatcher as S. Report's IFIP input/output calls are external mechanisms per the systems file, classed here as H for harness input/output and P for stage constants; x1's corresponding procedures are its own core I/O.

## Record coverage and access

There are 45 behaviour records with 75 physical stages. P08 stages are recorded twice, with "'`reading` closed/open, producing 114 outcome entries. All 60 original cost/storage records (100 stages) were compared against the matching behaviour run. The verbatim answers, observed state, printed stage output and execution classifications agree, so `mode_differences` is empty. No P07–P08 raw-rerun-m2 records, INVALID records, harness faults, limits, errors before stage end, or unreached stages are present. `rerun-m2-log.tsv` does not exist in this clone. Null/unavailable measurements were not converted to zero. Zero suspended/resumable work stated from the program'"'s observed state is distinct from an unavailable storage measurement.

Report/x1's budget process recreates earlier stages as documented, despite the incremental posing label. That is recorded in observations, not called manual intervention. x1sim receives P08 stages into a live process. Exhausted-input errors after an emitted [end] are documented harness shutdown and do not change the completed stage to error. No earlier explicit no-solution conclusion is withdrawn; under the closed interpretation the mathematical valid set changes when the definition becomes available, but the program had only printed its pending state.

Files read were confined to the allowed evidence: the five root specification/protocol files; the permitted problem files; systems/algol-60/README.md; the harness README, ALGOL README, S-mechanisms and relevant QUESTIONS text, stages.json and record.schema.json; the report P07/P08 program sources inspected above; all three configurations' P07/P08 constants; the batch text manifest and corresponding frozen token TSVs (including aliases); the 105 P07/P08 raw JSON records; and batch-log.tsv. Directory/file inventories were confined to allowed directories. Files generated in this output directory were also read for checking. **No file outside the permitted list was read, and no prohibited material was encountered accidentally.** In particular, the source repository was not modified, and no author README/audit, other classifier's classes, earlier batch results, variants, calibration, reviews, transcripts, other system directories or external files were opened.

## Totals

Distinct-text token totals (16 texts, 17,531 tokens): **P 2,971; C 414; R 3,122; S 0; H 11,024**. Expanding shared texts to all 30 program paths gives P 6,783; C 795; R 6,393; S 0; H 22,602 (36,573 tokens). Expanded figures repeat shared code and are not additional independently classed texts.

Across the 114 entries including both P08 readings: **114 complete** under the denotational convention explained above; 39 explicit, 18 solved form, 57 residual. Residuals: 3 reduced, 33 reducible, 21 inconsistency undetected. Execution: 57 finished and 57 suspended. There are no mode classification differences, harness faults or unreached stages. The check scripts verify exact token coverage, all 30 shared-text paths, every logged run, both readings of every P08 stage, and the record-to-behaviour comparisons.
